newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares risk further falls.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares risk further falls.

text.p: Belgian shares were seen extending their consolidation pattern on Friday, with players divided over whether the index would remain in its current overall uptrend or was in for a more substantial fall.
"We fear the consolidation may last a couple of days - we've reached a kind of plateau - after that there may be a downturn. The short term is gloomy and indices in Europe are way a" one dealer said.
The Bel-20 index closed on Thursday just 1.03 points or 0.06 percent higher at 1,811.18 after trading in a six-point range all day.
Retailers were prominent with dollar-sensitive Delhaize down 1.1 percent at 1,795 after losing 2.7 percent on Wednesday.

One dealer said Delhaize had been looking expensive in terms of fundamentals and noted buying in rivals, notably Colruyt which rose 1.3 percent to 13,175. Belgium's other major retail group GIB climbed 1.2 percent to 1,340.
Interest in the two retailers was also boosted by recent statistices showing private consumption was set to climb further in 1997, the dealer added.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert succumbed to a third day of profit taking after its recent rally begun in September.
